<div class="card-body">
'''Imperial Trooper Guard''' is a [[Dark]] [[Character]] ([[Imperial]]) from [[Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game (Japanese)|Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game (Japanese)]].
<nowiki />
<h2>Title</h2>
<span lang="ja">帝国軍警備兵員</span>
<h2>Card Text</h2>
<span lang="ja">移動できない。＊攻撃時は、戦闘力＝０で、防御時は、戦闘力＝４となる。</span><ref name="jp1-face">Japanese text as on the [[:File:Japanese-Premiere-PSA-01-Face.jpg|Japanese Premiere printed face]] of [[Imperial Trooper Guard (Japanese)]]; checked line by line against this Two-Player face, which prints the same text.</ref>
<ref name="jp-face">[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-Two-Player-Imperial-Trooper-Guard-C1G.jpg|This Two-Player printed face]].</ref>
<h2>Lore</h2>
''<span lang="ja">戦術や武器に長けたエリート兵士。デス・スター配属のタジス・ドゥアミンなどがその典型例で、重要拠点に配置されている。</span>''
<h2>Translation of Japanese Text</h2>
'''Title:''' Imperial guard personnel.

'''Card text:''' Cannot move. *When attacking, power = 0; when defending, power = 4.

'''Lore:''' Elite soldiers skilled in tactics and weapons. Tajis Durmin, assigned to the Death Star, is a typical example; they are stationed at important locations.

'''Comparison with the English printing:''' The English lore specifies guarding key areas of the Death Star. The Japanese says they are stationed at important locations, while identifying Tajis Durmin as assigned to the Death Star. The Japanese game text uses the shorter expressions ‘when attacking’ and ‘when defending’ for the English printing's offensive and defensive battles.
<h2>Notes</h2>
Japanese-language printing of [[Imperial Trooper Guard]] in [[Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game (Japanese)]].<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 44, 105. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="jp-face" />
